summary: The change adds a Secret Manager–backed email allowlist. It limits sign-in on the staging control plane and marks production sessions with `stagingAccess`, and the desktop app uses that flag to decide whether to show Help > Use Staging. The plumbing for the staging-testers flag is sound and tested. Changes are still needed for three reasons: the sign-in allowlist turns a failed list read into a signed-out session, which deletes saved desktop tokens; list refreshes add an untimed Secret Manager call to every authenticated request in production; and the allowlist enforcement has no tests (21 changed lines are uncovered).

findings.body: `stillAllowed` treats a failed allowlist read the same as "not allowed". In `SignInAllowlist.allows`, a failed read with no cached list returns an Error, which happens on every new Cloud Run instance until the first read succeeds. `getSession` then returns `undefined`, and `auth.session` answers `{ status: "signed-out" }`. When the desktop app sees that answer, `ControlPlaneAuth.getSessionUnqueued` calls `sessionStore.remove()` and clears the token. As a result, one transient Secret Manager failure on a cold staging instance signs out every staging user who connects during that window, and their saved session is lost. A read failure must surface as an error (for example, `getSession` returns the Error so the RPC fails with a 500), not as a signed-out session. Revoking access for users removed from the list should only happen when the list was actually read.

The list refresh runs inside the request. Every caller of `getSession` (each RPC, each workspace proxy request, each socket ticket) can end up waiting for `readGcpSecret`. That function has no timeout, and production now calls it through `hasStagingAccess` just to show a menu item. There are three problems:
1. Concurrent calls after the list expires each start their own read; nothing shares the in-flight refresh.
2. When a refresh fails but a cached list exists, `readAt` is not updated, so during a Secret Manager outage every request makes a new read instead of backing off.
3. A slow or hung read stalls production authentication for a cosmetic feature.
Fix: share a single in-flight refresh, and once a list exists, serve it while refreshing in the background. Also record the time of failed attempts so retries back off, and put a timeout on the read.

The staging sign-in restriction is a security control, and none of it is exercised: the `signInHooks` user and session create hooks (`signInHooks.ts` lines 13, 17, 24, 38–47), `findUserEmail` (`AuthService.ts` lines 116 and 145–155), `stillAllowed` (lines 361–363), and the check in `createWorkspaceSocketTicket` (line 372). Every temp test starts the control plane without `signInAllowlistSecretId`. The coverage-exempt note on the Postgres branch says the SQLite branch is "tested with the hooks", but no such test exists. Add tests that configure `signInAllowlistSecretId` and verify that the allowlist enforces access.

These changed lines are uncovered:
- The `signIn` branch that passes the session to `StagingToggle` (`registerDesktopApi.ts` lines 88–90).
- `readControlPlaneSecret` (`packages/config/src/controlPlane.ts` line 326), which every temp test mocks out.

The e2e test `stagingToggleMenu.e2e.test.ts` only asserts `visible: false` in a test build. The item was already hidden there before this change because the mode is not Production, so the test cannot show that `observe` changes the menu. Cover these paths with tests that would fail if the wiring broke.

testRequests.target: apps/control-plane/src/auth/signInHooks.ts + AuthService.ts:116,145-155 — with signInAllowlistSecretId set, creating a user or session for an unlisted email fails with NOT_INVITED, and a listed email (mixed case) succeeds
testRequests.rationale: The hooks that enforce staging sign-in have no test, and neither does the SQLite `findUserEmail` query they call.

testRequests.target: AuthService.getSession / createWorkspaceSocketTicket (AuthService.ts:331, 361-363, 372) — after an email is removed from the list and the list refreshes, `auth.session` returns signed-out and no socket ticket is issued; a listed user still gets a session
testRequests.rationale: Checks that sessions are revoked when an email leaves the list. This is currently uncovered.

testRequests.target: AuthService.getSession when the allowlist read fails with no cached list — must not report signed-out (see F1)
testRequests.rationale: Guards against desktop users being signed out by a transient Secret Manager error.

testRequests.target: SignInAllowlist.allows — a failed refresh keeps the last good list, and a later successful refresh replaces it (use the injected `now`)
testRequests.rationale: The keep-last-good branch and the refresh timing have no direct test.
